content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: 10% elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate (hosted) across eu-west-1 starting ~10:02 UTC. Error signature: "kv-cache-miss->oom" in runtime logs. Paging @oncall.

tara: Acked. I’m oncall for SRE this shift. Triage in thread. Quick ask: which customers are impacted and is there an active rollback? :eyes:

mike: I’m seeing spike in token generation failures tied to model-variant rwd-neo-350m-quant. Routes to fallback (rwd-neo-350m) are healthy. Customer impact: approximately 12% of requests from 3 enterprise keys are hitting the failing variant due to canary routing.

jess: tagging @product - which rollouts were active? We had a canary for quantized kernels this morning A/B.

anand: That canary started at 09:30 UTC. Policy: 5% traffic canary, but autoscale + routing pushed it to ~18% for short windows due to burst traffic.

natalie: Noted. I’ve paused the canary in the console (UI action). Will that stop new users from hitting the variant?

mike: Pausing stops new rollout assignments but active sessions still routed. Need immediate routing override or revert to previous model variant for canary group.

tara: Mitigation options:
- Quick: route traffic for the three affected API keys to fallback variant (scoped routing override).
- Safer: full revert of canary model build (needs infra approval, ~6min).
- Emergency: scale up pod count for quantized variant (may hide OOM but could cost and not fix root).

mike: I can push the scoped routing override now. Plan: add routing rule matching key IDs -> fallback variant for 1h, monitor 10m, then remove if stable. Owner: mike.

jess: I’ll coordinate customer comms if impact visible on dashboards. @natalie hold on any public msg until we see mitigation results.

mike: Executing override. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl route override --selector "api_key in (key_abc,key_xyz,key_def)" --model rwd-neo-350m --duration 60m
```

mike: Done. Routing rule applied. Dumping recent logs for the failing variant (tail 200):
```
[2026-03-07T10:01:21Z] model=rwd-neo-350m-quant worker=4 status=alloc memory=8.2G err=kv-cache-miss
[2026-03-07T10:01:23Z] model=rwd-neo-350m-quant worker=4 status=oom alloc=8.8G
[2026-03-07T10:01:27Z] model=rwd-neo-350m-quant worker=7 status=alloc memory=8.2G err=kv-cache-miss
[2026-03-07T10:02:05Z] model=rwd-neo-350m fallback route applied for keys key_abc,key_xyz,key_def
```

anand: Hypotheses:
1) Quantized kernel introduced a memory regression under certain sequence length distributions -> OOMs.
2) Canary autoscaling/routing bug increased percent traffic to canary beyond intended -> exposed edge case.
3) Upstream runtime change (kernel selection) + reduced mem headroom on certain hardware combo.

tara: Let’s track tests and owners in-thread:
- H1 (memory regression): owner mike. Test: run synthetic load with seq-len distribution matching production (70% short, 30% long) on rwd-neo-350m-quant in staging with identical compile flags.
- H2 (routing bug): owner anand. Test: verify rollout controller metrics and reproduce traffic spike with traffic-sim tool.
- H3 (kernel selection): owner jess + runtime team. Test: compare kernel selection logs between healthy and failing workers; reproduce by forcing kernel fallback.

mike: Starting the synthetic load now against staging quantized build. I’ll post results in 10m.

oncall-rotation-bot: Handoff reminder: tara will hand off to jess at 11:00 UTC. Please include status + next steps.

tara: Current status for handoff: routing override applied, observed immediate drop in 5xx for affected keys from 12%->0.5% within 2 minutes. Mitigation confirmed working. Active mitigation window until 11:05 UTC. Mike is running reproduction tests.

jess: Thanks. I’ll take over at 11:00. For now, I’ll open an experiment PR to rollback the canary build (small revert) so we can fast-apply if reproduction shows memory regression. Owner: jess.

mike: Synthetic load (10m) shows OOM reproduction when >25% requests have sequence length >1024. At smaller seq lengths, quantized variant is OK. Logs attached above. Conclusion: H1 likely.

anand: Rollout controller audit: There was a brief surge due to burst_override heuristic triggering additional canary assignments for sessions older than 5m. That explains traffic bump. So H2 contributed to exposure but root cause is H1.

jess: Plan:
- Short-term: keep scoped routing override until we either revert canary or deploy a patched quant kernel.
- Medium: cut a rollback PR now, test in staging. If tests fail, rollback blocked and we escalate to kernel patch.
- Long: add sequence-length gating for quantized variants in rollout policy.

natalie: I'll draft a customer status update saying we identified a model-level memory regression impacting a small set of enterprise keys, mitigation applied (traffic routed to fallback), and working on a rollback. QA: can we give ETA?

tara: ETA: rollback PR in 20-30m, then ~15m for validation, so conservative ETA 60m for full lift of routing override if rollback approved.

jess: PR opened: revert-quant-kernel-20260307 (#4243). Running CI tests now. If CI green, plan to deploy to canary and validate.

mike: CI shows regression test fail reproducing OOM in canary build. Pushing logs to the ticket.

jess: Because regression reproduces, we will not deploy. Escalating to runtime team for a kernel fix. Assigned to runtime squad; owner here: runtime-lead (out of thread).

tara: Handoff note for jess: routing override remains in place. Monitor 5xx and memory metrics. If any re-escalation, tag me.

jess: Taking over. Current incident state: mitigated but not resolved; scope: small set of enterprise keys; root cause: quantized kernel memory regression exposed by brief canary traffic surge. Next steps: runtime patch + staged redeploy, add rollout gating for seq-length, postmortem. Owning: jess for next 12h.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=P1->P2 (mitigated). New incident link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-20260307-1432

natalie: Drafted customer message and queued for review from jess.

mike: Closing note: uploaded reproduction script and perf traces to the incident ticket.

jess: Thanks everyone. I’ll post a follow-up when runtime patch ETA available. :thumbsup:
